title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page continues the analysis begun on p.544 of four homomorphisms (33)-(36) attached to Grothendieck's group M~_{0,3}. This group consists of outer automorphisms of the profinite fundamental group pi^_{0,3} of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity} that preserve the classes of the loop (inertia) subgroups, with the S_3 symmetry built in. It is a Grothendieck-Teichmuller-type group. The four targets are:
- (33) S_0M~ -> B'_0(Z^) = Z^* ⋉ Z^, the profinite 'ax+b' group, a Borel-type subgroup of GL_2;
- (34) M~ -> GL(2,Z^)/±1;
- (35)-(36) maps to the adelic unit tori (mod ±1) of Q(j), with j a cube root of unity, and of Q(i).
The two tori are the centralizers in GL_2 of the order-3 and order-2 symmetries rho and sigma.

What this page does. Using the decomposition (40), S_0M~ = M~[0] · S^+^_{0,3} (semidirect product), with (33) trivial on the second factor, describing (33) reduces to describing M~[0] -> B'_0(Z^). The margin note says exactly this.

Grothendieck then recalls work from §45 and §46 III:
- An element of M~ is given by a triple (alpha, beta, gamma).
- u depends only on the image of the 'cocycle' xi = alpha·rho(alpha)^{-1} in SL(2,Z^). The text adds 'not on SL(2,Z^)'' (presumably the derived subgroup), i.e. abelian-level data suffice.
- Writing xi = (A B; C D), formula (41) gives u = (1/D, B/D; 0, 1).
- Writing the matrix of alpha as (a b; c d) with ad - bc = eps' = ±1, formula (42) gives eps'D = c^2+cd+d^2 and eps'B = ac+bd+bc.

Check of (42). Take R = (0 -1; 1 -1), of order 3, and compute xi = alpha R alpha^{-1} R^{-1}. One gets
- xi_12 = eps'(ac+bd+bc),
- xi_22 = eps'(c^2+cd+d^2),
- xi_21 = eps'(ac+ad+bd-c^2-cd-d^2).
So (42) is correct.

The norm form. D is ± the norm form of Z[omega] evaluated at (c,d). So u is defined only where this norm is a unit in Z^. This constraint must come from membership in M~[0], i.e. normalizing the inertia subgroup L_0 pi. That is the link to the Q(j) torus in (35).

The margin cocycle condition. The condition xi·rho(xi)·rho^2(xi) = ±1 holds automatically when xi has the coboundary form alpha R alpha^{-1} R^{-1}: the product telescopes to alpha R^3 alpha^{-1} R^{-3}.

Methodological remark. Grothendieck notes that none of this needs the unfinished foundations on profinite groups; 'somewhat fine computations' suffice.

Normalization (43). The description lets him define the normalized subgroup M~(0) ⊂ M~[0] by u ∈ Gamma_0(Z^), i.e. B = 0, i.e. ac+bd+bc = 0. This is a normalization condition analogous to choosing a canonical representative modulo inner automorphisms by the inertia L_0 pi. On p.545 it yields the semidirect decompositions M~[0] = M~(0)·L_0 pi and M~ = M~(0)·S^+^, and the computation of the GL_2 map (34) on M~(0).
errors: Not an error but a redundancy: the condition xi·rho(xi)·rho^2(xi) = ±1 written in the margin is automatic for xi = alpha·rho(alpha)^{-1} with rho^3 = ±1, since the product telescopes. Grothendieck's '!' may signal exactly this realization.
Gap: (41) requires D = ±(c^2+cd+d^2) to be a unit of Z^. The page does not state why this holds on M~[0]; presumably it follows from the normalizing condition, but this is not shown here.

ideas.what: Homomorphism from the (S_3-extended) GT-type automorphism group of pi^_{0,3}, restricted to the inertia normalizer, to the profinite affine group Z^*⋉Z^, given explicitly by the matrix formula u = (1/D, B/D; 0, 1) from the cocycle xi = alpha·rho(alpha)^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: abelianized / metabelian characters of GT (cyclotomic character and Kummer-type cocycle); action on the abelianization of the free profinite group F^_2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (pro-l braid / Jacobi sum characters), Drinfeld (GT), Lochak-Schneps, Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's unpublished 'Longue Marche' continuation (cote 140-3); the general program appears in Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Explicit formulas D = ±(c^2+cd+d^2), B = ±(ac+bd+bc) in terms of the abelianized matrix of alpha
ideas.modern_name: norm form of Z[omega] / conjugation by the order-3 element of SL_2

ideas.what: Normalization condition B = 0 (u ∈ Gamma_0(Z^)) defining a canonical subgroup M~(0) and splitting M~[0] = M~(0)·L_0 pi
ideas.modern_name: normalized GT elements (f in the commutator subgroup) / choosing a representative of an outer automorphism modulo inertia

ideas.what: Maps to the adelic unit tori of Q(cube root of 1) and Q(i), as centralizers of the order-3 and order-2 symmetries
ideas.modern_name: CM tori at the orbifold points j=0 and j=1728 of M_{1,1}; Galois action on the CM elliptic curves

missed.claim: Grothendieck systematically links the S_3-extended GT-type group of P^1-{0,1,inf} to the CM tori of Q(omega) and Q(i), via the Borel group B'_0 and the order-3/order-2 symmetries, with explicit norm-form formulas. This is an early, explicit version of the link between GT and the special (CM) points of M_{1,1}.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This connection was later studied separately (Nakamura, Lochak-Nakamura-Schneps, Ihara on GT and SL_2(Z^)). Grothendieck's explicit four-homomorphism package (33)-(36) and the normalization B=0 could be compared with modern normalizations of GT, but it is largely recoverable from known theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The computation is correct and fits a coherent unpublished construction: four homomorphisms from the GT-type group to Borel, GL_2 and CM tori, plus a normalization splitting. The underlying ideas are known in the GT literature, though this particular explicit packaging is not published.
transcription_corrections: Archive page number is 483; Grothendieck's own numbering is not visible on this page (neighbours are 544 and 545).

In (42), the first line is ε'D = (c^2+cd+d^2) with a trailing ε struck out.
The marginal formula is ξρ(ξ)ρ^2(ξ) = ±1 (cocycle condition), preceded by something like 'ou en conditions pour'.
